v.rationale: Both suites pass (impl-1: 42 tests, impl-2: 43). They share the same core design: createOrFirst for dedup, a queued job with WithoutOverlapping and RateLimited, Backoff/MaxExceptions attributes, retryUntil, failed() and MassPrunable. They differ in correctness of the domain logic. In impl-1, order transitions are atomic conditional updates. Refunds are deduplicated by the provider refund id, and the job requires the refund amount. Failed events can be retried. Its only real gaps are that a signed event with empty data gets a 422, and extra payload keys are dropped on storage. In impl-2, refunds are keyed by webhook event id, so the same refund under two event ids creates two rows (probe confirmed). It silently records the full order amount when the payload has no amount, and it marks unpaid orders as refunded. A failed event can't be reprocessed at all, not through queue:retry and not through redelivery. impl-2 does have somewhat better intake validation and nice extras (onOneServer, DeleteWhenMissingModels, lock-holding test), but those don't outweigh the refund-handling bugs. impl-1 adds a stuck-event recovery command the task didn't ask for, which costs a little on simplicity. It still ranks first.
